   194→bool recordStereoToPSRAM() {
   195→  uint32_t samples_written = 0;
   196→  uint32_t last_percent = 0;
   197→  unsigned long start_time = millis();
   198→
   199→  while (samples_written < STEREO_SAMPLES) {
   200→    // Blink LED
   201→    if ((millis() / 200) % 2 == 0) {
   202→      digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH);
   203→    } else {
   204→      digitalWrite(LED_PIN, LOW);
   205→    }
   206→
   207→    // Read I2S
   208→    size_t bytes_read = 0;
   209→    if (i2s_read(I2S_NUM_0, i2s_buffer, BUFFER_SIZE * sizeof(int32_t),
   210→                 &bytes_read, portMAX_DELAY) != ESP_OK) {
   211→      return false;
   212→    }
   213→
   214→    // Convert and store
   215→    int samples_read = bytes_read / sizeof(int32_t);
   216→    for (int i = 0; i < samples_read && samples_written < STEREO_SAMPLES; i++) {
   217→      stereo_buffer[samples_written++] = (int16_t)(i2s_buffer[i] >> 16);
   218→    }
   219→
   220→    // Progress
   221→    uint32_t percent = (samples_written * 100) / STEREO_SAMPLES;
   222→    if (percent != last_percent && percent % 10 == 0) {
   223→      Serial.printf("Progress: %u%% (%u / %u samples)\n",
   224→                    percent, samples_written, STEREO_SAMPLES);
   225→      last_percent = percent;
   226→    }
   227→  }
   228→
   229→  Serial.printf("\nRecorded: %u samples in %lu ms\n", samples_written, millis() - start_time);
   230→  return true;
   231→}
   232→
   233→void downmixHybrid() {
   234→  float left_energy = 0.0f;
   235→  float right_energy = 0.0f;
   236→  const float ENERGY_DECAY = 0.95f;
   237→  const float MIN_WEIGHT = 0.30f;  // Minimum 30% per channel
   238→  const float MAX_WEIGHT = 0.70f;  // Maximum 70% per channel
   239→  const float GAIN_BOOST = 4.0f;   // 4x volume boost (compensates for 9dB hardware gain)
   240→
   241→  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < MONO_SAMPLES; i++) {
   242→    int16_t left = stereo_buffer[i * 2];
   243→    int16_t right = stereo_buffer[i * 2 + 1];
   244→
   245→    // Track energy of each channel
   246→    left_energy = left_energy * ENERGY_DECAY + abs(left) * (1.0f - ENERGY_DECAY);
   247→    right_energy = right_energy * ENERGY_DECAY + abs(right) * (1.0f - ENERGY_DECAY);
   248→
   249→    // Calculate raw weights
   250→    float total_energy = left_energy + right_energy;
   251→    float left_weight = (total_energy > 0) ? (left_energy / total_energy) : 0.5f;
   252→
   253→    // Constrain to 30%-70% range
   254→    if (left_weight < MIN_WEIGHT) left_weight = MIN_WEIGHT;
   255→    if (left_weight > MAX_WEIGHT) left_weight = MAX_WEIGHT;
   256→
   257→    float right_weight = 1.0f - left_weight;
   258→
   259→    // Weighted mix with gain boost and clipping protection
   260→    int32_t mixed = (int32_t)(left * left_weight + right * right_weight) * GAIN_BOOST;
   261→    if (mixed > 32767) mixed = 32767;
   262→    if (mixed < -32768) mixed = -32768;
   263→    mono_buffer[i] = (int16_t)mixed;
   264→  }
   265→}
   266→
   267→void normalizeAudio() {
   268→  // Find peak level in recording
   269→  int16_t peak = 0;
   270→  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < MONO_SAMPLES; i++) {
   271→    int16_t abs_val = abs(mono_buffer[i]);
   272→    if (abs_val > peak) peak = abs_val;
   273→  }
   274→
   275→  Serial.printf("Peak level: %d / 32767 (%.1f%%)\n", peak, (peak * 100.0f) / 32767.0f);
   276→
   277→  // Calculate normalization gain to maximize volume
   278→  if (peak > 0) {
   279→    float norm_gain = 32000.0f / peak;  // Leave small headroom (32000 instead of 32767)
   280→
   281→    // Limit max boost to 8x to avoid amplifying noise too much
   282→    if (norm_gain > 8.0f) norm_gain = 8.0f;
   283→
   284→    Serial.printf("Applying normalization: %.2fx gain\n", norm_gain);
   285→
   286→    // Apply normalization
   287→    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < MONO_SAMPLES; i++) {
   288→      int32_t normalized = (int32_t)(mono_buffer[i] * norm_gain);
   289→      if (normalized > 32767) normalized = 32767;
   290→      if (normalized < -32768) normalized = -32768;
   291→      mono_buffer[i] = (int16_t)normalized;
   292→    }
   293→  } else {
   294→    Serial.println("WARNING: Recording is silent (peak = 0)!");
   295→  }
   296→}
   297→
   298→void playMonoBuffer() {
   299→  size_t bytes_written = 0;
   300→  static unsigned long last_print = 0;
   301→
   302→  // Play entire mono buffer
   303→  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < MONO_SAMPLES; i += BUFFER_SIZE) {
   304→    uint32_t samples_to_write = min((uint32_t)BUFFER_SIZE, MONO_SAMPLES - i);
   305→
   306→    i2s_write(I2S_NUM_1, &mono_buffer[i], samples_to_write * sizeof(int16_t),
   307→              &bytes_written, portMAX_DELAY);
   308→
   309→    // Print status every ~2 seconds
   310→    if (millis() - last_print > 2000) {
   311→      Serial.printf("Playing... sample %u / %u\n", i, MONO_SAMPLES);
   312→      last_print = millis();
   313→    }
   314→  }
   315→
   316→  Serial.println("Playback complete, looping...\n");
   317→}
   318→
   319→void error_blink() {
   320→  while(1) {
   321→    digitalWrite(LED_PIN, !digitalRead(LED_PIN));
   322→    delay(200);
   323→  }
   324→}

     1→# Record, Downmix, and Playback Loop
     2→
     3→## Overview
     4→
     5→This sketch demonstrates a complete audio capture and playback pipeline:
     6→1. **Records 30 seconds** of stereo audio from dual INMP441 microphones
     7→2. **Downmixes to mono** using HYBRID algorithm (adaptive + width)
     8→3. **Plays back** continuously through MAX98357A speaker
     9→
    10→## Hardware Requirements
    11→
    12→- ESP32-S3-LCD-2 board
    13→- 2× INMP441 MEMS microphones
    14→- 1× MAX98357A I2S amplifier module
    15→- 2× 1W flat mag speakers (4-8 ohm)

    32→                        │                      │

    82→
    83→## Downmix Algorithm: HYBRID
    84→
    85→The HYBRID downmix algorithm combines the best of two approaches:
    86→
    87→- **Adaptive weighting**: Favors the microphone with stronger signal (clarity)
    88→- **30%-70% constraint**: Ensures both channels always contribute (width)
    89→
    90→This prevents the "interruption" feeling when blocking one mic while maintaining clarity and reducing background noise compared to simple averaging.
    91→

   100→  - Mic #2: L/R → **3.3V** (right channel)
   101→
   102→- **Speaker**: Connect to I2S1 (GPIO 6, 7, 8)

   184→int16_t scaled = mono_buffer[i] * 2;  // 2x gain (may clip!)
   185→i2s_write(I2S_NUM_1, &scaled, ...);
   186→```
   187→
   188→### Test Downmix Quality
   189→
   190→The HYBRID algorithm should provide:
   191→- ✅ Clear, intelligible voice
   192→- ✅ Captures from multiple directions
   193→- ✅ No "interruption" when blocking one mic
   194→- ✅ Less background noise than simple average
   195→
   196→## Troubleshooting
   197→
   198→### No audio from speaker
   199→
   200→- Check MAX98357A wiring (especially BCLK, LRC, DIN)
   201→- Verify speaker is connected to SPK+/SPK-
   202→- Try connecting SD pin to VIN (enable amplifier)
   203→- Check Serial Monitor for I2S1 initialization errors
   204→
   205→### Distorted/clipped audio
   206→
   207→- Lower GAIN pin setting (try Float = 9dB)
   208→- Check speaker impedance (4-8 ohm required)
   209→- Verify 5V power is stable
   210→
   211→### Quiet playback
   212→
   213→- Increase GAIN pin setting (connect to VDD = 15dB)
   214→- Use 5V instead of 3.3V for VIN
   215→- Use 4-ohm speaker instead of 8-ohm
   216→- **Software gain**: Increase `GAIN_BOOST` to 6.0f or 8.0f (line 235 in .ino)
   217→- **Recording level**: Speak very loudly into mics during recording, position mics 5-10cm from mouth
   218→
   219→### Recording noise/static
   220→
   221→- Check microphone wiring (especially L/R pins)
   222→- Verify both mics are powered (3.3V to VDD)
   223→- Ensure solid I2S connections (GPIO 2, 4, 18)
   224→- Try different microphones if one is defective
   225→
   226→### Playback loops too fast/slow
   227→
   228→- Sample rate mismatch - ensure both I2S buses use 16kHz
   229→- Check `SAMPLE_RATE` constant is 16000
   230→
   231→## How It Works
   232→
   233→### 1. Dual I2S Buses
   234→
   235→ESP32-S3 has multiple I2S peripherals:
   236→- **I2S_NUM_0**: Microphones (RX mode)
   237→- **I2S_NUM_1**: Speaker (TX mode)
   238→
   239→These run independently and can operate simultaneously.
   240→
   241→### 2. Recording Phase
   242→
   243→```
   244→I2S0 (mics) → i2s_buffer (32-bit) → stereo_buffer (16-bit, PSRAM)
   245→```
   246→
   247→Captures 30 seconds of stereo audio (left + right interleaved).
   248→
   249→### 3. Downmix Phase
   250→
   251→```
   252→stereo_buffer → HYBRID algorithm → mono_buffer (PSRAM)
   253→```
   254→
   255→Applies adaptive weighting with 30%-70% constraints.
   256→
   257→### 4. Playback Phase
   258→
   259→```
   260→mono_buffer → I2S1 (speaker) → Loop forever
   261→```
   262→
   263→Continuously plays the mono recording.
   264→
   265→## Next Steps
   266→
   267→Once you've verified the basic loop works:
   268→
   269→1. **Add voice activity detection (VAD)** - Only record when voice detected
   270→2. **Implement push-to-talk** - Button to trigger recording
   271→3. **Add effects** - Reverb, echo, pitch shift
   272→4. **Stream to WiFi** - Send audio over network
   273→5. **Add compression** - OPUS codec for smaller files
   274→6. **Dual direction** - Record while playing (walkie-talkie mode)
   275→
   276→## Technical References
   277→
   278→- **ESP32-S3 I2S**: [ESP-IDF I2S Documentation](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/latest/esp32s3/api-reference/peripherals/i2s.html)
   279→- **INMP441 Datasheet**: Omnidirectional I2S MEMS Microphone
   280→- **MAX98357A Datasheet**: I2S Class D Amplifier
   281→- **Hybrid Downmix**: Adaptive weighting with minimum contribution per channel
   282→
   283→---
   284→
   285→**Power Tip:** For battery operation, use 3.3V for MAX98357A VIN to reduce current draw. Volume will be lower but adequate for close listening!
   286→

    43→void onSrEvent(sr_event_t event, int command_id, int phrase_id) {
    44→  switch (event) {
    45→    case SR_EVENT_WAKEWORD: Serial.println("WakeWord Detected!"); break;
    46→    case SR_EVENT_WAKEWORD_CHANNEL:
    47→      Serial.printf("WakeWord Channel %d Verified!\n", command_id);
    48→      ESP_SR.setMode(SR_MODE_COMMAND);  // Switch to Command detection
    49→      break;
    50→    case SR_EVENT_TIMEOUT:
    51→      Serial.println("Timeout Detected!");
    52→      ESP_SR.setMode(SR_MODE_WAKEWORD);  // Switch back to WakeWord detection
    53→      break;
    54→    case SR_EVENT_COMMAND:
    55→      Serial.printf("Command %d Detected! %s\n", command_id, sr_commands[phrase_id].str);
    56→      switch (command_id) {
    57→        case SR_CMD_TURN_ON_THE_LIGHT:  digitalWrite(LIGHT_PIN, HIGH); break;
    58→        case SR_CMD_TURN_OFF_THE_LIGHT: digitalWrite(LIGHT_PIN, LOW); break;
    59→        case SR_CMD_START_FAN:          digitalWrite(FAN_PIN, HIGH); break;
    60→        case SR_CMD_STOP_FAN:           digitalWrite(FAN_PIN, LOW); break;
    61→        default:                        Serial.println("Unknown Command!"); break;
    62→      }
    63→      ESP_SR.setMode(SR_MODE_COMMAND);  // Allow for more commands to be given, before timeout
    64→      // ESP_SR.setMode(SR_MODE_WAKEWORD); // Switch back to WakeWord detection
    65→      break;
    66→    default: Serial.println("Unknown Event!"); break;
    67→  }
    68→}
    69→
    70→void setup() {
    71→  Serial.begin(115200);
    72→
    73→  pinMode(LIGHT_PIN, OUTPUT);
    74→  digitalWrite(LIGHT_PIN, LOW);
    75→  pinMode(FAN_PIN, OUTPUT);
    76→  digitalWrite(FAN_PIN, LOW);
    77→
    78→  i2s.setPins(I2S_PIN_BCK, I2S_PIN_WS, -1, I2S_PIN_DIN);
    79→  i2s.setTimeout(1000);
    80→  i2s.begin(I2S_MODE_STD, 16000, I2S_DATA_BIT_WIDTH_16BIT, I2S_SLOT_MODE_STEREO);
    81→
    82→  ESP_SR.onEvent(onSrEvent);
    83→  ESP_SR.begin(i2s, sr_commands, sizeof(sr_commands) / sizeof(sr_cmd_t), SR_CHANNELS_STEREO, SR_MODE_WAKEWORD, SR_INPUT_FORMAT);
    84→}
    85→
    86→void loop() {}
    87→

    91→  EventGroupHandle_t event_group;
    92→} sr_data_t;
    93→
    94→static int SR_CHANNEL_NUM = 3;
    95→
    96→static srmodel_list_t *models = NULL;
    97→static sr_data_t *g_sr_data = NULL;
    98→
    99→esp_err_t sr_set_mode(sr_mode_t mode);
   100→
   101→void sr_handler_task(void *pvParam) {
   102→  while (true) {
   103→    sr_result_t result;
   104→    if (xQueueReceive(g_sr_data->result_que, &result, portMAX_DELAY) != pdTRUE) {
   105→      continue;
   106→    }
   107→
   108→    if (WAKENET_DETECTED == result.wakenet_mode) {
   109→      if (g_sr_data->user_cb) {
   110→        g_sr_data->user_cb(g_sr_data->user_cb_arg, SR_EVENT_WAKEWORD, -1, -1);
   111→      }
   112→      continue;
   113→    }
   114→
   115→    if (WAKENET_CHANNEL_VERIFIED == result.wakenet_mode) {
   116→      if (g_sr_data->user_cb) {
   117→        g_sr_data->user_cb(g_sr_data->user_cb_arg, SR_EVENT_WAKEWORD_CHANNEL, result.command_id, -1);
   118→      }
   119→      continue;
   120→    }
   121→
   122→    if (ESP_MN_STATE_DETECTED == result.state) {
   123→      if (g_sr_data->user_cb) {
   124→        g_sr_data->user_cb(g_sr_data->user_cb_arg, SR_EVENT_COMMAND, result.command_id, result.phrase_id);
   125→      }
   126→      continue;
   127→    }
   128→
   129→    if (ESP_MN_STATE_TIMEOUT == result.state) {
   130→      if (g_sr_data->user_cb) {
   131→        g_sr_data->user_cb(g_sr_data->user_cb_arg, SR_EVENT_TIMEOUT, -1, -1);
   132→      }
   133→      continue;
   134→    }
   135→  }
   136→  vTaskDelete(NULL);
   137→}
   138→
   139→static void audio_feed_task(void *arg) {
   140→  size_t bytes_read = 0;
   141→  int audio_chunksize = g_sr_data->afe_handle->get_feed_chunksize(g_sr_data->afe_data);
   142→  log_i("audio_chunksize=%d, feed_channel=%d", audio_chunksize, SR_CHANNEL_NUM);
   143→
   144→  /* Allocate audio buffer and check for result */
   145→  int16_t *audio_buffer = heap_caps_malloc(audio_chunksize * sizeof(int16_t) * SR_CHANNEL_NUM, MALLOC_CAP_INTERNAL | MALLOC_CAP_8BIT);
   146→  if (NULL == audio_buffer) {
   147→    esp_system_abort("No mem for audio buffer");
   148→  }
   149→  g_sr_data->afe_in_buffer = audio_buffer;
   150→
   151→  while (true) {
   152→    EventBits_t bits = xEventGroupGetBits(g_sr_data->event_group);
   153→    if (NEED_DELETE & bits) {
   154→      xEventGroupSetBits(g_sr_data->event_group, FEED_DELETED);
   155→      break;
   156→    }
   157→    if (PAUSE_FEED & bits) {
   158→      xEventGroupWaitBits(g_sr_data->event_group, PAUSE_FEED | RESUME_FEED, 1, 1, portMAX_DELAY);
   159→    }
   160→
   161→    /* Read audio data from I2S bus */
   162→    //ToDo: handle error
   163→    if (g_sr_data->fill_cb == NULL) {
   164→      vTaskDelay(100);
   165→      continue;
   166→    }
   167→    esp_err_t err = g_sr_data->fill_cb(
   168→      g_sr_data->fill_cb_arg, (char *)audio_buffer, audio_chunksize * g_sr_data->i2s_rx_chan_num * sizeof(int16_t), &bytes_read, portMAX_DELAY
   169→    );
   170→    if (err != ESP_OK) {
   171→      vTaskDelay(100);
   172→      continue;
   173→    }
   174→
   175→    /* Channel Adjust */
   176→    if (g_sr_data->i2s_rx_chan_num == 1) {
   177→      for (int i = audio_chunksize - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
   178→        audio_buffer[i * SR_CHANNEL_NUM + 2] = 0;
   179→        audio_buffer[i * SR_CHANNEL_NUM + 1] = 0;
   180→        audio_buffer[i * SR_CHANNEL_NUM + 0] = audio_buffer[i];
   181→      }
   182→    } else if (g_sr_data->i2s_rx_chan_num == 2) {
   183→      for (int i = audio_chunksize - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
   184→        audio_buffer[i * SR_CHANNEL_NUM + 2] = 0;
   185→        audio_buffer[i * SR_CHANNEL_NUM + 1] = audio_buffer[i * 2 + 1];
   186→        audio_buffer[i * SR_CHANNEL_NUM + 0] = audio_buffer[i * 2 + 0];
   187→      }
   188→    } else {
   189→      vTaskDelay(100);
   190→      continue;
   191→    }
   192→
   193→    /* Feed samples of an audio stream to the AFE_SR */
   194→    g_sr_data->afe_handle->feed(g_sr_data->afe_data, audio_buffer);
   195→    vTaskDelay(2);
   196→  }
   197→  vTaskDelete(NULL);
   198→}
   199→
   200→static void audio_detect_task(void *arg) {
   201→  int afe_chunksize = g_sr_data->afe_handle->get_fetch_chunksize(g_sr_data->afe_data);
   202→  int mu_chunksize = g_sr_data->multinet->get_samp_chunksize(g_sr_data->model_data);
   203→  assert(mu_chunksize == afe_chunksize);
   204→  log_i("------------detect start------------");
   205→
   206→  while (true) {
   207→    EventBits_t bits = xEventGroupGetBits(g_sr_data->event_group);
   208→    if (NEED_DELETE & bits) {
   209→      xEventGroupSetBits(g_sr_data->event_group, DETECT_DELETED);
   210→      break;
   211→    }
   212→    if (PAUSE_DETECT & bits) {
   213→      xEventGroupWaitBits(g_sr_data->event_group, PAUSE_DETECT | RESUME_DETECT, 1, 1, portMAX_DELAY);
   214→    }
   215→
   216→    afe_fetch_result_t *res = g_sr_data->afe_handle->fetch(g_sr_data->afe_data);
   217→    if (!res || res->ret_value == ESP_FAIL) {
   218→      continue;
   219→    }
   220→
   221→    if (g_sr_data->mode == SR_MODE_WAKEWORD) {
   222→      if (res->wakeup_state == WAKENET_DETECTED) {
   223→        log_d("wakeword detected");
   224→        sr_result_t result = {
   225→          .wakenet_mode = WAKENET_DETECTED,
   226→          .state = ESP_MN_STATE_DETECTING,
   227→          .command_id = 0,
   228→          .phrase_id = 0,
   229→        };
   230→        xQueueSend(g_sr_data->result_que, &result, 0);
   231→      } else if (res->wakeup_state == WAKENET_CHANNEL_VERIFIED) {
   232→        sr_set_mode(SR_MODE_OFF);
   233→        log_d("AFE_FETCH_CHANNEL_VERIFIED, channel index: %d", res->trigger_channel_id);
   234→        sr_result_t result = {
   235→          .wakenet_mode = WAKENET_CHANNEL_VERIFIED,
   236→          .state = ESP_MN_STATE_DETECTING,
   237→          .command_id = res->trigger_channel_id,
   238→          .phrase_id = 0,
   239→        };
   240→        xQueueSend(g_sr_data->result_que, &result, 0);
   241→      }
   242→    }
   243→
   244→    if (g_sr_data->mode == SR_MODE_COMMAND) {
   245→
   246→      esp_mn_state_t mn_state = ESP_MN_STATE_DETECTING;
   247→      mn_state = g_sr_data->multinet->detect(g_sr_data->model_data, res->data);
   248→
   249→      if (ESP_MN_STATE_DETECTING == mn_state) {
   250→        continue;
   251→      }
   252→
   253→      if (ESP_MN_STATE_TIMEOUT == mn_state) {
   254→        sr_set_mode(SR_MODE_OFF);
   255→        log_d("Time out");
   256→        sr_result_t result = {
   257→          .wakenet_mode = WAKENET_NO_DETECT,
   258→          .state = mn_state,
   259→          .command_id = 0,
   260→          .phrase_id = 0,
   261→        };
   262→        xQueueSend(g_sr_data->result_que, &result, 0);
   263→        continue;
   264→      }
   265→
   266→      if (ESP_MN_STATE_DETECTED == mn_state) {
   267→        sr_set_mode(SR_MODE_OFF);
   268→        esp_mn_results_t *mn_result = g_sr_data->multinet->get_results(g_sr_data->model_data);
   269→        for (int i = 0; i < mn_result->num; i++) {
   270→          log_d("TOP %d, command_id: %d, phrase_id: %d, prob: %f", i + 1, mn_result->command_id[i], mn_result->phrase_id[i], mn_result->prob[i]);
   271→        }
   272→
   273→        int sr_command_id = mn_result->command_id[0];
   274→        int sr_phrase_id = mn_result->phrase_id[0];
   275→        log_d("Detected command : %d, phrase: %d", sr_command_id, sr_phrase_id);
   276→        sr_result_t result = {
   277→          .wakenet_mode = WAKENET_NO_DETECT,
   278→          .state = mn_state,
   279→          .command_id = sr_command_id,
   280→          .phrase_id = sr_phrase_id,
   281→        };
   282→        xQueueSend(g_sr_data->result_que, &result, 0);
   283→        continue;
   284→      }
   285→      log_e("Exception unhandled");
   286→    }
   287→  }
   288→  vTaskDelete(NULL);
   289→}
   290→
   291→esp_err_t sr_set_mode(sr_mode_t mode) {
   292→  ESP_RETURN_ON_FALSE(NULL != g_sr_data, ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE, "SR is not running");
   293→  switch (mode) {
   294→    case SR_MODE_OFF:
   295→      if (g_sr_data->mode == SR_MODE_WAKEWORD) {
   296→        g_sr_data->afe_handle->disable_wakenet(g_sr_data->afe_data);
   297→      }
   298→      break;
   299→    case SR_MODE_WAKEWORD:
   300→      if (g_sr_data->mode != SR_MODE_WAKEWORD) {
   301→        g_sr_data->afe_handle->enable_wakenet(g_sr_data->afe_data);
   302→      }
   303→      break;
   304→    case SR_MODE_COMMAND:
   305→      if (g_sr_data->mode == SR_MODE_WAKEWORD) {
   306→        g_sr_data->afe_handle->disable_wakenet(g_sr_data->afe_data);
   307→      }
   308→      break;
   309→    default: return ESP_FAIL;
   310→  }
   311→  g_sr_data->mode = mode;
   312→  return ESP_OK;
   313→}
   314→
   315→esp_err_t sr_start(
   316→  sr_fill_cb fill_cb, void *fill_cb_arg, sr_channels_t rx_chan, sr_mode_t mode, const char *input_format, const sr_cmd_t sr_commands[], size_t cmd_number,
   317→  sr_event_cb cb, void *cb_arg
   318→) {
   319→  esp_err_t ret = ESP_OK;
   320→  ESP_RETURN_ON_FALSE(NULL == g_sr_data, ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE, "SR already running");
   321→
   322→  g_sr_data = heap_caps_calloc(1, sizeof(sr_data_t), MALLOC_CAP_INTERNAL | MALLOC_CAP_8BIT);
   323→  ESP_RETURN_ON_FALSE(NULL != g_sr_data, ESP_ERR_NO_MEM, "Failed create sr data");
   324→
   325→  g_sr_data->result_que = xQueueCreate(3, sizeof(sr_result_t));
   326→  ESP_GOTO_ON_FALSE(NULL != g_sr_data->result_que, ESP_ERR_NO_MEM, err, "Failed create result queue");
   327→
   328→  g_sr_data->event_group = xEventGroupCreate();
   329→  ESP_GOTO_ON_FALSE(NULL != g_sr_data->event_group, ESP_ERR_NO_MEM, err, "Failed create event_group");
   330→
   331→  BaseType_t ret_val;
   332→  g_sr_data->user_cb = cb;
   333→  g_sr_data->user_cb_arg = cb_arg;
   334→  g_sr_data->fill_cb = fill_cb;
   335→  g_sr_data->fill_cb_arg = fill_cb_arg;
   336→  g_sr_data->i2s_rx_chan_num = rx_chan + 1;
   337→  g_sr_data->mode = mode;
   338→
   339→  // Init Model
   340→  log_d("init model");
   341→  models = esp_srmodel_init("model");
   342→
   343→  // Load WakeWord Detection
   344→  afe_config_t *afe_config = afe_config_init(input_format, models, AFE_TYPE_SR, AFE_MODE_LOW_COST);
   345→  g_sr_data->afe_handle = esp_afe_handle_from_config(afe_config);
   346→  log_d("load wakenet '%s'", afe_config->wakenet_model_name);
   347→  g_sr_data->afe_data = g_sr_data->afe_handle->create_from_config(afe_config);
   348→  afe_config_free(afe_config);
   349→
   350→  // Load Custom Command Detection
   351→  char *mn_name = esp_srmodel_filter(models, ESP_MN_PREFIX, ESP_MN_ENGLISH);
   352→  log_d("load multinet '%s'", mn_name);
   353→  g_sr_data->multinet = esp_mn_handle_from_name(mn_name);
   354→  log_d("load model_data '%s'", mn_name);
   355→  g_sr_data->model_data = g_sr_data->multinet->create(mn_name, 5760);
   356→
   357→  // Add commands
   358→  esp_mn_commands_alloc((esp_mn_iface_t *)g_sr_data->multinet, (model_iface_data_t *)g_sr_data->model_data);
   359→  log_i("add %d commands", cmd_number);
   360→  for (size_t i = 0; i < cmd_number; i++) {
   361→    esp_mn_commands_add(sr_commands[i].command_id, (char *)(sr_commands[i].phoneme));
   362→    log_i("  cmd[%d] phrase[%d]:'%s'", sr_commands[i].command_id, i, sr_commands[i].str);
   363→  }
   364→
   365→  // Load commands
   366→  esp_mn_error_t *err_id = esp_mn_commands_update();
   367→  if (err_id) {
   368→    for (int i = 0; i < err_id->num; i++) {
   369→      log_e("err cmd id:%d", err_id->phrases[i]->command_id);
   370→    }
   371→  }
   372→
   373→  //Start tasks
   374→  log_d("start tasks");
   375→  ret_val = xTaskCreatePinnedToCore(&audio_feed_task, "SR Feed Task", 4 * 1024, NULL, 5, &g_sr_data->feed_task, 0);
   376→  ESP_GOTO_ON_FALSE(pdPASS == ret_val, ESP_FAIL, err, "Failed create audio feed task");
   377→  vTaskDelay(10);
   378→  ret_val = xTaskCreatePinnedToCore(&audio_detect_task, "SR Detect Task", 8 * 1024, NULL, 5, &g_sr_data->detect_task, 1);
   379→  ESP_GOTO_ON_FALSE(pdPASS == ret_val, ESP_FAIL, err, "Failed create audio detect task");
   380→  ret_val = xTaskCreatePinnedToCore(&sr_handler_task, "SR Handler Task", 6 * 1024, NULL, configMAX_PRIORITIES - 1, &g_sr_data->handle_task, 1);
   381→  //ret_val = xTaskCreatePinnedToCore(&sr_handler_task, "SR Handler Task", 6 * 1024, NULL, configMAX_PRIORITIES - 1, &g_sr_data->handle_task, 0);
   382→  ESP_GOTO_ON_FALSE(pdPASS == ret_val, ESP_FAIL, err, "Failed create audio handler task");
   383→
   384→  return ESP_OK;
   385→err:
   386→  sr_stop();
   387→  return ret;
   388→}
   389→
   390→esp_err_t sr_stop(void) {
   391→  ESP_RETURN_ON_FALSE(NULL != g_sr_data, ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE, "SR is not running");
   392→
   393→  /**
   394→     * Waiting for all task stopped
   395→     * TODO: A task creation failure cannot be handled correctly now
   396→     * */
   397→  vTaskDelete(g_sr_data->handle_task);
   398→  xEventGroupSetBits(g_sr_data->event_group, NEED_DELETE);
   399→  xEventGroupWaitBits(g_sr_data->event_group, NEED_DELETE | FEED_DELETED | DETECT_DELETED, 1, 1, portMAX_DELAY);
   400→
   401→  if (g_sr_data->result_que) {
   402→    vQueueDelete(g_sr_data->result_que);
   403→    g_sr_data->result_que = NULL;
   404→  }
   405→
   406→  if (g_sr_data->event_group) {
   407→    vEventGroupDelete(g_sr_data->event_group);
   408→    g_sr_data->event_group = NULL;
   409→  }
   410→
   411→  if (g_sr_data->model_data) {
   412→    g_sr_data->multinet->destroy(g_sr_data->model_data);
   413→  }
   414→
   415→  if (g_sr_data->afe_data) {
   416→    g_sr_data->afe_handle->destroy(g_sr_data->afe_data);
   417→  }
   418→
   419→  if (g_sr_data->afe_in_buffer) {
   420→    heap_caps_free(g_sr_data->afe_in_buffer);
   421→  }
   422→
   423→  heap_caps_free(g_sr_data);
   424→  g_sr_data = NULL;
   425→  return ESP_OK;
   426→}
   427→
   428→esp_err_t sr_pause(void) {
   429→  ESP_RETURN_ON_FALSE(NULL != g_sr_data, ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE, "SR is not running");
   430→  xEventGroupSetBits(g_sr_data->event_group, PAUSE_FEED | PAUSE_DETECT);
   431→  return ESP_OK;
   432→}
   433→
   434→esp_err_t sr_resume(void) {
   435→  ESP_RETURN_ON_FALSE(NULL != g_sr_data, ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE, "SR is not running");
   436→  xEventGroupSetBits(g_sr_data->event_group, RESUME_FEED | RESUME_DETECT);
   437→  return ESP_OK;
   438→}

```ino
/*
 * ESP-SR Wake Word Detection Demo
 *
 * Demonstrates the ESP32-S3 built-in speech recognition library.
 * Detects wake word "Hi ESP" and custom voice commands.
 *
 * Hardware:
 * =========
 * INMP441 Microphones (I2S0 RX):
 *   Mic #1 (LEFT):  L/R -> GND
 *   Mic #2 (RIGHT): L/R -> 3.3V
 *   Both share: BCK=GPIO2, WS=GPIO4, DIN=GPIO18
 *
 * LED Feedback (GPIO 1):
 *   - Blink fast: Listening for wake word
 *   - Solid ON: Wake word detected, listening for command
 *   - Off briefly: Command executed
 *
 * IMPORTANT - Board Settings:
 * ===========================
 * 1. Board: ESP32S3 Dev Module
 * 2. Partition Scheme: ESP SR 16M (3MB APP/7MB SPIFFS/2.9MB MODEL)
 * 3. PSRAM: OPI PSRAM
 * 4. Flash Size: 16MB
 * 5. Flash Mode: DIO (or QIO if supported)
 *
 * The ESP_SR library requires the "esp_sr_16" partition scheme which
 * includes a dedicated partition for the speech recognition models.
 * Without this partition, the library will fail to initialize.
 *
 * Wake Word:
 * ==========
 * Default wake word is "Hi ESP" (built into the model)
 *
 * Voice Commands (after wake word):
 * =================================
 * - "Turn on the light" / "Switch on the light"
 * - "Turn off the light" / "Switch off the light" / "Go dark"
 * - "Red" / "Green" / "Blue"
 * - "Start"
 * - "Stop"
 *
 * Usage:
 * ======
 * 1. Upload sketch with correct partition scheme
 * 2. Open Serial Monitor at 115200 baud
 * 3. Say "Hi ESP" to wake up
 * 4. After wake word detected, speak a command within 6 seconds
 * 5. After command or timeout, returns to wake word listening mode
 */

#include "ESP_I2S.h"
#include "ESP_SR.h"

// Microphone pins (I2S0) - matches speaker_mic_combo config
#define I2S_PIN_BCK  2
#define I2S_PIN_WS   4
#define I2S_PIN_DIN  18

// LED for feedback
#define LED_PIN 1

// Input format for ESP_SR
// MM = dual microphone channels (stereo)
// MN = single mic + unused channel
// M = single mono mic
#define SR_INPUT_FORMAT "MM"

// I2S interface
I2SClass i2s;

// Command IDs
enum {
  SR_CMD_LIGHT_ON,
  SR_CMD_LIGHT_OFF,
  SR_CMD_RED,
  SR_CMD_GREEN,
  SR_CMD_BLUE,
  SR_CMD_START,
  SR_CMD_STOP,
};

// Voice commands with phoneme translations
// Generated using: python3 gen_sr_commands.py "command1,alias1;command2"
// Phonemes are ESP-SR specific encoding - see ESP_SR/tools/gen_sr_commands.py
static const sr_cmd_t sr_commands[] = {
  {SR_CMD_LIGHT_ON,  "Turn on the light",   "TkN nN jc LiT"},
  {SR_CMD_LIGHT_ON,  "Switch on the light", "SWgp nN jc LiT"},
  {SR_CMD_LIGHT_OFF, "Turn off the light",  "TkN eF jc LiT"},
  {SR_CMD_LIGHT_OFF, "Switch off the light","SWgp eF jc LiT"},
  {SR_CMD_LIGHT_OFF, "Go dark",             "Gb DnRK"},
  {SR_CMD_RED,       "Red",                 "RfD"},
  {SR_CMD_GREEN,     "Green",               "GRmN"},
  {SR_CMD_BLUE,      "Blue",                "BLo"},
  {SR_CMD_START,     "Start",               "STnRT"},
  {SR_CMD_STOP,      "Stop",                "STnP"},
};

// State tracking
volatile bool wake_detected = false;
volatile bool command_mode = false;
unsigned long last_blink = 0;
bool led_state = false;

void onSrEvent(sr_event_t event, int command_id, int phrase_id) {
  switch (event) {
    case SR_EVENT_WAKEWORD:
      Serial.println("\n*** WAKE WORD DETECTED! ***");
      wake_detected = true;
      break;

    case SR_EVENT_WAKEWORD_CHANNEL:
      Serial.printf("Wake word verified on channel %d\n", command_id);
      Serial.println("Listening for command...\n");
      command_mode = true;
      digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH);  // Solid LED = listening
      ESP_SR.setMode(SR_MODE_COMMAND);
      break;

    case SR_EVENT_TIMEOUT:
      Serial.println("Command timeout - returning to wake word mode\n");
      command_mode = false;
      ESP_SR.setMode(SR_MODE_WAKEWORD);
      break;

    case SR_EVENT_COMMAND:
      Serial.printf("Command detected: %s (id=%d, phrase=%d)\n",
                    sr_commands[phrase_id].str, command_id, phrase_id);

      // Handle command
      handleCommand(command_id);

      // Brief LED off to acknowledge
      digitalWrite(LED_PIN, LOW);
      delay(100);
      digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH);

      // Allow more commands (or switch back to wake word)
      ESP_SR.setMode(SR_MODE_COMMAND);
      break;

    default:
      Serial.printf("Unknown event: %d\n", event);
      break;
  }
}

void handleCommand(int cmd_id) {
  switch (cmd_id) {
    case SR_CMD_LIGHT_ON:
      Serial.println("  -> Light ON");
      break;
    case SR_CMD_LIGHT_OFF:
      Serial.println("  -> Light OFF");
      break;
    case SR_CMD_RED:
      Serial.println("  -> Color: RED");
      break;
    case SR_CMD_GREEN:
      Serial.println("  -> Color: GREEN");
      break;
    case SR_CMD_BLUE:
      Serial.println("  -> Color: BLUE");
      break;
    case SR_CMD_START:
      Serial.println("  -> START action");
      break;
    case SR_CMD_STOP:
      Serial.println("  -> STOP action");
      break;
    default:
      Serial.println("  -> Unknown command");
      break;
  }
}

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  delay(1000);

  pinMode(LED_PIN, OUTPUT);
  digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH);

  Serial.println("\n========================================");
  Serial.println("ESP-SR Wake Word Detection Demo");
  Serial.println("========================================\n");

  // Check PSRAM
  Serial.printf("Total PSRAM: %u bytes\n", ESP.getPsramSize());
  Serial.printf("Free PSRAM: %u bytes\n", ESP.getFreePsram());
  Serial.printf("Total Heap: %u bytes\n", ESP.getHeapSize());
  Serial.printf("Free Heap: %u bytes\n\n", ESP.getFreeHeap());

  // Initialize I2S for microphones
  Serial.print("Initializing I2S (microphones)... ");
  i2s.setPins(I2S_PIN_BCK, I2S_PIN_WS, -1, I2S_PIN_DIN);  // -1 = no DOUT
  i2s.setTimeout(1000);

  if (!i2s.begin(I2S_MODE_STD, 16000, I2S_DATA_BIT_WIDTH_16BIT, I2S_SLOT_MODE_STEREO)) {
    Serial.println("FAILED!");
    Serial.println("Check I2S wiring and pins.");
    errorBlink();
  }
  Serial.println("OK");

  // Initialize ESP_SR
  Serial.print("Initializing ESP-SR... ");

  ESP_SR.onEvent(onSrEvent);

  if (!ESP_SR.begin(i2s, sr_commands, sizeof(sr_commands) / sizeof(sr_cmd_t),
                    SR_CHANNELS_STEREO, SR_MODE_WAKEWORD, SR_INPUT_FORMAT)) {
    Serial.println("FAILED!");
    Serial.println("\nESP_SR initialization failed. Common causes:");
    Serial.println("1. Wrong partition scheme - select 'ESP SR 16M' in Arduino IDE");
    Serial.println("2. Insufficient memory - need 16MB flash with PSRAM");
    Serial.println("3. Model partition not found at offset 0xD10000");
    Serial.println("\nCheck your board settings and try again.");
    errorBlink();
  }
  Serial.println("OK\n");

  // Print help
  Serial.println("========================================");
  Serial.println("Ready! Say 'Hi ESP' to wake up.");
  Serial.println("========================================");
  Serial.println("\nAvailable commands after wake word:");
  for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(sr_commands) / sizeof(sr_cmd_t); i++) {
    Serial.printf("  - '%s'\n", sr_commands[i].str);
  }
  Serial.println("\nListening for wake word...\n");
}

void loop() {
  // Blink LED while listening for wake word (not in command mode)
  if (!command_mode) {
    if (millis() - last_blink > 500) {
      last_blink = millis();
      led_state = !led_state;
      digitalWrite(LED_PIN, led_state);
    }
  }

  // Reset wake detected flag
  if (wake_detected) {
    wake_detected = false;
  }

  delay(10);
}

void errorBlink() {
  while (1) {
    digitalWrite(LED_PIN, !digitalRead(LED_PIN));
    delay(100);
  }
}

```

```md
# ESP-SR Wake Word Detection Demo

Demonstrates the ESP32-S3 built-in speech recognition library for wake word detection and voice command recognition.

## Requirements

### Hardware
- ESP32-S3-LCD-2 board (or any ESP32-S3 with 16MB flash + PSRAM)
- INMP441 MEMS microphones (1 or 2)

### Arduino IDE Settings

**CRITICAL**: You must use the `ESP SR 16M` partition scheme!

| Setting | Value |
|---------|-------|
| Board | ESP32S3 Dev Module |
| Partition Scheme | **ESP SR 16M (3MB APP/7MB SPIFFS/2.9MB MODEL)** |
| PSRAM | OPI PSRAM |
| Flash Size | 16MB |
| Flash Mode | DIO (or QIO) |

The ESP_SR library requires a special partition layout that includes a dedicated ~2.9MB partition for the speech recognition models (wakenet + multinet). Without this partition scheme, the library will fail to initialize.

## Wiring

### Single Microphone Setup

\```
INMP441                 ESP32-S3
────────                ────────
VDD  ──────────────────→ 3.3V
GND  ──────────────────→ GND
SCK  ──────────────────→ GPIO 2 (BCK)
WS   ──────────────────→ GPIO 4 (WS)
SD   ──────────────────→ GPIO 18 (DIN)
L/R  ──────────────────→ GND (left channel)
\```

For single mic, change `SR_INPUT_FORMAT` to `"MN"` and `SR_CHANNELS_STEREO` to `SR_CHANNELS_MONO`.

### Dual Microphone Setup (Stereo)

\```
ESP32-S3          INMP441 #1 (LEFT)      INMP441 #2 (RIGHT)
────────          ─────────────────      ──────────────────
3.3V ─────────┬── VDD                    VDD
              │
GND ──────────┼── GND ───────────┬────── GND
              │                  │
GPIO 2 ───────┼── SCK ───────────┼────── SCK
GPIO 4 ────────┼── WS ───────────┼────── WS
GPIO 18 ──────┴── SD ────────────┴────── SD
                  │                      │
                  L/R → GND              L/R → 3.3V
                    (LEFT)                 (RIGHT)
\```

## Wake Word

The default built-in wake word is **"Hi ESP"** (pronounced "Hi E-S-P").

Say it clearly with a brief pause before speaking a command.

## Voice Commands

After the wake word is detected, you have ~6 seconds to speak a command:

| Command | Aliases | Action |
|---------|---------|--------|
| "Turn on the light" | "Switch on the light" | Light ON |
| "Turn off the light" | "Switch off the light", "Go dark" | Light OFF |
| "Red" | - | Color RED |
| "Green" | - | Color GREEN |
| "Blue" | - | Color BLUE |
| "Start" | - | Start action |
| "Stop" | - | Stop action |

## LED Feedback

| LED State | Meaning |
|-----------|---------|
| Slow blink (500ms) | Listening for wake word |
| Solid ON | Wake word detected, listening for command |
| Fast blink (100ms) | Error - check serial output |

## Serial Output

Open Serial Monitor at 115200 baud to see:
- Initialization status
- Wake word detections
- Command recognitions
- Error messages

## Customizing Commands

To add custom commands, you need to generate phoneme strings using the `gen_sr_commands.py` tool:

\```bash
# Install dependency
pip3 install g2p_en

# Generate phonemes
cd ~/.arduino15/packages/esp32/hardware/esp32/3.3.2/libraries/ESP_SR/tools
python3 gen_sr_commands.py "Hello world;Goodbye"
\```

This outputs the `sr_cmd_t` struct entries with phoneme encodings.

## Troubleshooting

### "ESP_SR initialization failed"

1. **Wrong partition scheme**: Make sure "ESP SR 16M" is selected in Arduino IDE
2. **Insufficient flash**: Need 16MB flash for the model partition
3. **No PSRAM**: Enable "OPI PSRAM" in board settings

### No response to wake word

1. Check microphone wiring (BCK, WS, DIN pins)
2. Verify 3.3V power to microphone
3. Try speaking louder/closer
4. Check L/R pin is connected to GND (for left channel)

### Commands not recognized

1. Speak clearly after wake word
2. Wait for "Listening for command..." message
3. Don't speak too fast
4. Try the exact phrase from the command table

## Technical Details

- Sample rate: 16 kHz
- Bit depth: 16-bit
- Wake word model: WakeNet (built-in "Hi ESP")
- Command model: MultiNet (English)
- AFE mode: Low cost (single-channel processing)

## References

- [ESP-SR Documentation](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-sr/en/latest/)
- [ESP32 Arduino ESP_SR Library](https://github.com/espressif/arduino-esp32/tree/master/libraries/ESP_SR)
- [ESP-IDF Speech Recognition](https://github.com/espressif/esp-sr)

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-5-20251101)**_

Done! Created `workbench/tests/esp_sr_test/` with the ESP-SR wake word detection demo.

## Key Points

**Critical Arduino IDE Settings:**
| Setting | Value |
|---------|-------|
| Partition Scheme | **ESP SR 16M** (contains ~2.9MB model partition) |
| PSRAM | OPI PSRAM |
| Flash Size | 16MB |

The ESP_SR library embeds Espressif's WakeNet (wake word) and MultiNet (command recognition) models, which require a dedicated flash partition.

**Wake Word:** "Hi ESP"

**Voice Commands (after wake):**
- "Turn on/off the light"
- "Red" / "Green" / "Blue"
- "Start" / "Stop"

**Mic Pins (from your speaker_mic_combo):**
- BCK = GPIO 2
- WS = GPIO 4
- DIN = GPIO 18

**How it works:**
1. ESP_SR uses the new `ESP_I2S` library (Stream-based)
2. Audio feeds into AFE (Audio Front End) for noise reduction
3. WakeNet detects "Hi ESP"
4. After wake, MultiNet recognizes commands using phoneme matching
5. 6-second timeout returns to wake word mode

**Customization:** To add custom commands, use the `gen_sr_commands.py` tool in the ESP_SR library to generate phoneme strings from English phrases.

   154→ * N to represent an unknown or unused channel

/*
 * ESP-SR Wake Word Detection (SD Card Model Loading)
 *
 * Loads speech recognition models from SD card into PSRAM at runtime.
 * No special partition scheme required - uses your existing partition layout.
 *
 * Hardware:
 * =========
 * INMP441 Microphones (I2S0 RX):
 *   Mic #1 (LEFT):  L/R -> GND
 *   Mic #2 (RIGHT): L/R -> 3.3V
 *   Both share: BCK=GPIO2, WS=GPIO4, DIN=GPIO18
 *
 * SD Card (SPI):
 *   Uses existing SPI bus shared with LCD
 *
 * Setup:
 * ======
 * 1. Copy 'srmodels.bin' to SD card root directory
 *    Source: ~/.arduino15/packages/esp32/tools/esp32-arduino-libs/
 *            idf-release_v5.5-07e9bf49-v1/esp32s3/esp_sr/srmodels.bin
 *
 * 2. Board Settings (Arduino IDE):
 *    - Board: ESP32S3 Dev Module
 *    - Partition: Your existing scheme (e.g., 16MB 3MB APP/9MB FATFS)
 *    - PSRAM: OPI PSRAM
 *    - Flash Size: 16MB
 *
 * Wake Word: "Hi ESP"
 *
 * Commands (after wake word):
 * - "Turn on the light" / "Switch on the light"
 * - "Turn off the light" / "Switch off the light"
 * - "Red" / "Green" / "Blue"
 * - "Start" / "Stop"
 */

#include <SPI.h>
#include <SD.h>
#include "ESP_I2S.h"

// ESP-SR low-level headers
#include "esp_afe_sr_iface.h"
#include "esp_afe_sr_models.h"
#include "esp_mn_iface.h"
#include "esp_mn_models.h"
#include "esp_wn_iface.h"
#include "esp_wn_models.h"
#include "esp_mn_speech_commands.h"
#include "model_path.h"

// Microphone pins (I2S0)
#define I2S_PIN_BCK  2
#define I2S_PIN_WS   4
#define I2S_PIN_DIN  18

// SD Card CS pin (shared SPI with LCD)
#define SD_CS_PIN    41

// LED for feedback
#define LED_PIN 1

// Model file on SD card
#define MODEL_FILE "/srmodels.bin"

// Audio configuration
#define SAMPLE_RATE     16000
#define AUDIO_CHUNKSIZE 512

// Command IDs
enum {
  SR_CMD_LIGHT_ON,
  SR_CMD_LIGHT_OFF,
  SR_CMD_RED,
  SR_CMD_GREEN,
  SR_CMD_BLUE,
  SR_CMD_START,
  SR_CMD_STOP,
};

// Voice commands with phoneme translations
typedef struct {
  int command_id;
  const char* text;
  const char* phoneme;
} sr_command_t;

static const sr_command_t commands[] = {
  {SR_CMD_LIGHT_ON,  "Turn on the light",   "TkN nN jc LiT"},
  {SR_CMD_LIGHT_ON,  "Switch on the light", "SWgp nN jc LiT"},
  {SR_CMD_LIGHT_OFF, "Turn off the light",  "TkN eF jc LiT"},
  {SR_CMD_LIGHT_OFF, "Switch off the light","SWgp eF jc LiT"},
  {SR_CMD_LIGHT_OFF, "Go dark",             "Gb DnRK"},
  {SR_CMD_RED,       "Red",                 "RfD"},
  {SR_CMD_GREEN,     "Green",               "GRmN"},
  {SR_CMD_BLUE,      "Blue",                "BLo"},
  {SR_CMD_START,     "Start",               "STnRT"},
  {SR_CMD_STOP,      "Stop",                "STnP"},
};
static const int NUM_COMMANDS = sizeof(commands) / sizeof(commands[0]);

// Global state
I2SClass i2s;
uint8_t* model_data = nullptr;
srmodel_list_t* models = nullptr;
esp_afe_sr_iface_t* afe_handle = nullptr;
esp_afe_sr_data_t* afe_data = nullptr;
esp_mn_iface_t* multinet = nullptr;
model_iface_data_t* mn_model_data = nullptr;

// Task handles
TaskHandle_t feed_task_handle = nullptr;
TaskHandle_t detect_task_handle = nullptr;

// State
volatile bool is_wake_mode = true;
volatile bool running = true;

// Forward declarations
void feed_task(void* arg);
void detect_task(void* arg);
void handleCommand(int cmd_id);

bool loadModelFromSD() {
  Serial.print("Mounting SD card... ");

  if (!SD.begin(SD_CS_PIN)) {
    Serial.println("FAILED!");
    Serial.println("Check SD card is inserted and formatted as FAT32.");
    return false;
  }
  Serial.println("OK");

  Serial.printf("Opening %s... ", MODEL_FILE);
  File file = SD.open(MODEL_FILE, FILE_READ);
  if (!file) {
    Serial.println("FAILED!");
    Serial.println("Copy srmodels.bin to SD card root.");
    return false;
  }
  Serial.println("OK");

  size_t file_size = file.size();
  Serial.printf("Model size: %u bytes\n", file_size);

  Serial.print("Allocating PSRAM... ");
  model_data = (uint8_t*)ps_malloc(file_size);
  if (!model_data) {
    Serial.println("FAILED!");
    Serial.println("Not enough PSRAM.");
    file.close();
    return false;
  }
  Serial.println("OK");

  Serial.print("Loading model to PSRAM... ");
  size_t bytes_read = file.read(model_data, file_size);
  file.close();

  if (bytes_read != file_size) {
    Serial.printf("FAILED! (read %u of %u bytes)\n", bytes_read, file_size);
    free(model_data);
    model_data = nullptr;
    return false;
  }
  Serial.println("OK");

  // Parse model data
  Serial.print("Parsing models... ");
  models = srmodel_load(model_data);
  if (!models) {
    Serial.println("FAILED!");
    Serial.println("Invalid model file format.");
    free(model_data);
    model_data = nullptr;
    return false;
  }
  Serial.printf("OK (%d models found)\n", models->num);

  // List available models
  for (int i = 0; i < models->num; i++) {
    Serial.printf("  - %s\n", models->model_name[i]);
  }

  return true;
}

bool initAFE() {
  Serial.print("Initializing AFE... ");

  // Configure AFE for dual mic stereo input
  afe_config_t* afe_config = afe_config_init("MM", models, AFE_TYPE_SR, AFE_MODE_LOW_COST);
  if (!afe_config) {
    Serial.println("FAILED (config)!");
    return false;
  }

  // Get AFE handle and create instance
  afe_handle = esp_afe_handle_from_config(afe_config);
  if (!afe_handle) {
    Serial.println("FAILED (handle)!");
    afe_config_free(afe_config);
    return false;
  }

  afe_data = afe_handle->create_from_config(afe_config);
  afe_config_free(afe_config);

  if (!afe_data) {
    Serial.println("FAILED (data)!");
    return false;
  }

  Serial.println("OK");
  return true;
}

bool initMultinet() {
  Serial.print("Initializing MultiNet... ");

  // Find English multinet model
  char* mn_name = esp_srmodel_filter(models, ESP_MN_PREFIX, ESP_MN_ENGLISH);
  if (!mn_name) {
    Serial.println("FAILED! (no English model)");
    return false;
  }
  Serial.printf("using %s... ", mn_name);

  // Get multinet handle
  multinet = (esp_mn_iface_t*)esp_mn_handle_from_name(mn_name);
  if (!multinet) {
    Serial.println("FAILED (handle)!");
    return false;
  }

  // Create multinet instance
  mn_model_data = multinet->create(mn_name, 5760);
  if (!mn_model_data) {
    Serial.println("FAILED (create)!");
    return false;
  }

  // Add commands
  esp_mn_commands_alloc(multinet, mn_model_data);
  for (int i = 0; i < NUM_COMMANDS; i++) {
    esp_mn_commands_add(commands[i].command_id, (char*)commands[i].phoneme);
  }

  // Update command list
  esp_mn_error_t* err = esp_mn_commands_update();
  if (err) {
    Serial.printf("FAILED! (%d cmd errors)\n", err->num);
    return false;
  }

  Serial.println("OK");
  return true;
}

bool initI2S() {
  Serial.print("Initializing I2S... ");

  i2s.setPins(I2S_PIN_BCK, I2S_PIN_WS, -1, I2S_PIN_DIN);
  i2s.setTimeout(1000);

  if (!i2s.begin(I2S_MODE_STD, SAMPLE_RATE, I2S_DATA_BIT_WIDTH_16BIT, I2S_SLOT_MODE_STEREO)) {
    Serial.println("FAILED!");
    return false;
  }

  Serial.println("OK");
  return true;
}

void feed_task(void* arg) {
  int chunksize = afe_handle->get_feed_chunksize(afe_data);
  int total_channels = 3;  // AFE expects 3 channels internally

  // Allocate audio buffer
  int16_t* audio_buffer = (int16_t*)heap_caps_malloc(
    chunksize * sizeof(int16_t) * total_channels,
    MALLOC_CAP_INTERNAL | MALLOC_CAP_8BIT
  );

  if (!audio_buffer) {
    Serial.println("Feed task: buffer alloc failed!");
    vTaskDelete(NULL);
    return;
  }

  Serial.printf("Feed task started (chunksize=%d)\n", chunksize);

  while (running) {
    // Read stereo audio from I2S
    size_t bytes_read = i2s.readBytes((char*)audio_buffer, chunksize * 2 * sizeof(int16_t));

    if (bytes_read == 0) {
      vTaskDelay(10);
      continue;
    }

    // Expand stereo to 3-channel format (AFE requirement)
    // Move from back to front to avoid overwriting
    for (int i = chunksize - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
      audio_buffer[i * total_channels + 2] = 0;  // Reference channel (unused)
      audio_buffer[i * total_channels + 1] = audio_buffer[i * 2 + 1];  // Right mic
      audio_buffer[i * total_channels + 0] = audio_buffer[i * 2 + 0];  // Left mic
    }

    // Feed to AFE
    afe_handle->feed(afe_data, audio_buffer);
    vTaskDelay(2);
  }

  heap_caps_free(audio_buffer);
  vTaskDelete(NULL);
}

void detect_task(void* arg) {
  Serial.println("Detect task started");
  Serial.println("\nListening for wake word 'Hi ESP'...\n");

  while (running) {
    afe_fetch_result_t* res = afe_handle->fetch(afe_data);

    if (!res || res->ret_value == ESP_FAIL) {
      continue;
    }

    // Wake word mode
    if (is_wake_mode) {
      if (res->wakeup_state == WAKENET_DETECTED) {
        Serial.println("\n*** WAKE WORD DETECTED! ***");
        digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH);
      }
      else if (res->wakeup_state == WAKENET_CHANNEL_VERIFIED) {
        Serial.printf("Wake verified (channel %d)\n", res->trigger_channel_id);
        Serial.println("Listening for command...\n");

        // Switch to command mode
        is_wake_mode = false;
        afe_handle->disable_wakenet(afe_data);
      }
    }
    // Command mode
    else {
      esp_mn_state_t mn_state = multinet->detect(mn_model_data, res->data);

      if (mn_state == ESP_MN_STATE_DETECTING) {
        continue;
      }

      if (mn_state == ESP_MN_STATE_TIMEOUT) {
        Serial.println("Command timeout - returning to wake mode\n");
        is_wake_mode = true;
        afe_handle->enable_wakenet(afe_data);
        digitalWrite(LED_PIN, LOW);
      }
      else if (mn_state == ESP_MN_STATE_DETECTED) {
        esp_mn_results_t* mn_result = multinet->get_results(mn_model_data);

        int cmd_id = mn_result->command_id[0];
        int phrase_id = mn_result->phrase_id[0];

        Serial.printf("Command: '%s' (id=%d, conf=%.2f)\n",
                      commands[phrase_id].text, cmd_id, mn_result->prob[0]);

        handleCommand(cmd_id);

        // Brief LED flash
        digitalWrite(LED_PIN, LOW);
        vTaskDelay(100);
        digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH);

        // Stay in command mode for more commands
        // Or switch back: is_wake_mode = true; afe_handle->enable_wakenet(afe_data);
      }
    }
  }

  vTaskDelete(NULL);
}

void handleCommand(int cmd_id) {
  switch (cmd_id) {
    case SR_CMD_LIGHT_ON:  Serial.println("  -> Light ON");  break;
    case SR_CMD_LIGHT_OFF: Serial.println("  -> Light OFF"); break;
    case SR_CMD_RED:       Serial.println("  -> RED");       break;
    case SR_CMD_GREEN:     Serial.println("  -> GREEN");     break;
    case SR_CMD_BLUE:      Serial.println("  -> BLUE");      break;
    case SR_CMD_START:     Serial.println("  -> START");     break;
    case SR_CMD_STOP:      Serial.println("  -> STOP");      break;
    default:               Serial.println("  -> Unknown");   break;
  }
}

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  delay(1000);

  pinMode(LED_PIN, OUTPUT);
  digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH);

  Serial.println("\n========================================");
  Serial.println("ESP-SR Wake Word Demo (SD Card Models)");
  Serial.println("========================================\n");

  // Memory info
  Serial.printf("PSRAM: %u / %u bytes free\n", ESP.getFreePsram(), ESP.getPsramSize());
  Serial.printf("Heap:  %u / %u bytes free\n\n", ESP.getFreeHeap(), ESP.getHeapSize());

  // Load model from SD card
  if (!loadModelFromSD()) {
    errorBlink();
  }
  Serial.println();

  // Initialize I2S
  if (!initI2S()) {
    errorBlink();
  }

  // Initialize AFE (Audio Front End)
  if (!initAFE()) {
    errorBlink();
  }

  // Initialize MultiNet (command recognition)
  if (!initMultinet()) {
    errorBlink();
  }

  Serial.println();

  // Print available commands
  Serial.println("Voice commands (after wake word):");
  for (int i = 0; i < NUM_COMMANDS; i++) {
    Serial.printf("  - '%s'\n", commands[i].text);
  }
  Serial.println();

  // Start processing tasks
  xTaskCreatePinnedToCore(feed_task, "SR_Feed", 4096, NULL, 5, &feed_task_handle, 0);
  xTaskCreatePinnedToCore(detect_task, "SR_Detect", 8192, NULL, 5, &detect_task_handle, 1);

  Serial.println("========================================");
  Serial.println("Ready! Say 'Hi ESP' to wake up.");
  Serial.println("========================================\n");

  digitalWrite(LED_PIN, LOW);  // LED off = listening for wake word
}

void loop() {
  // Blink LED slowly when listening for wake word
  if (is_wake_mode) {
    static unsigned long last_blink = 0;
    if (millis() - last_blink > 1000) {
      last_blink = millis();
      digitalWrite(LED_PIN, !digitalRead(LED_PIN));
    }
  }

  delay(100);
}

void errorBlink() {
  Serial.println("\n*** INITIALIZATION FAILED ***");
  while (1) {
    digitalWrite(LED_PIN, !digitalRead(LED_PIN));
    delay(100);
  }
}

   275→void feed_task(void* arg) {
   276→  int chunksize = afe_handle->get_feed_chunksize(afe_data);
   277→  int total_channels = 3;  // AFE expects 3 channels internally
   278→
   279→  // Allocate audio buffer
   280→  int16_t* audio_buffer = (int16_t*)heap_caps_malloc(
   281→    chunksize * sizeof(int16_t) * total_channels,
   282→    MALLOC_CAP_INTERNAL | MALLOC_CAP_8BIT
   283→  );
   284→
   285→  if (!audio_buffer) {
   286→    Serial.println("Feed task: buffer alloc failed!");
   287→    vTaskDelete(NULL);
   288→    return;
   289→  }
   290→
   291→  Serial.printf("Feed task started (chunksize=%d)\n", chunksize);
   292→
   293→  while (running) {
   294→    // Read stereo audio from I2S
   295→    size_t bytes_read = i2s.readBytes((char*)audio_buffer, chunksize * 2 * sizeof(int16_t));
   296→
   297→    if (bytes_read == 0) {
   298→      vTaskDelay(10);
   299→      continue;
   300→    }
   301→
   302→    // Expand stereo to 3-channel format (AFE requirement)
   303→    // Move from back to front to avoid overwriting
   304→    for (int i = chunksize - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
   305→      audio_buffer[i * total_channels + 2] = 0;  // Reference channel (unused)
   306→      audio_buffer[i * total_channels + 1] = audio_buffer[i * 2 + 1];  // Right mic
   307→      audio_buffer[i * total_channels + 0] = audio_buffer[i * 2 + 0];  // Left mic
   308→    }
   309→
   310→    // Feed to AFE
   311→    afe_handle->feed(afe_data, audio_buffer);
   312→    vTaskDelay(2);
   313→  }
   314→
   315→  heap_caps_free(audio_buffer);
   316→  vTaskDelete(NULL);
   317→}
   318→
   319→void detect_task(void* arg) {
   320→  Serial.println("Detect task started");
   321→  Serial.println("\nListening for wake word 'Hi ESP'...\n");
   322→
   323→  while (running) {
   324→    afe_fetch_result_t* res = afe_handle->fetch(afe_data);
   325→
   326→    if (!res || res->ret_value == ESP_FAIL) {
   327→      continue;
   328→    }
   329→
   330→    // Wake word mode
   331→    if (is_wake_mode) {
   332→      if (res->wakeup_state == WAKENET_DETECTED) {
   333→        Serial.println("\n*** WAKE WORD DETECTED! ***");
   334→        digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH);
   335→      }
   336→      else if (res->wakeup_state == WAKENET_CHANNEL_VERIFIED) {
   337→        Serial.printf("Wake verified (channel %d)\n", res->trigger_channel_id);
   338→        Serial.println("Listening for command...\n");
   339→
   340→        // Switch to command mode
   341→        is_wake_mode = false;
   342→        afe_handle->disable_wakenet(afe_data);
   343→      }
   344→    }
   345→    // Command mode
   346→    else {
   347→      esp_mn_state_t mn_state = multinet->detect(mn_model_data, res->data);
   348→
   349→      if (mn_state == ESP_MN_STATE_DETECTING) {
   350→        continue;
   351→      }
   352→
   353→      if (mn_state == ESP_MN_STATE_TIMEOUT) {
   354→        Serial.println("Command timeout - returning to wake mode\n");
   355→        is_wake_mode = true;
   356→        afe_handle->enable_wakenet(afe_data);
   357→        digitalWrite(LED_PIN, LOW);
   358→      }
   359→      else if (mn_state == ESP_MN_STATE_DETECTED) {
   360→        esp_mn_results_t* mn_result = multinet->get_results(mn_model_data);
   361→
   362→        int cmd_id = mn_result->command_id[0];
   363→        int phrase_id = mn_result->phrase_id[0];
   364→
   365→        Serial.printf("Command: '%s' (id=%d, conf=%.2f)\n",
   366→                      commands[phrase_id].text, cmd_id, mn_result->prob[0]);
   367→
   368→        handleCommand(cmd_id);
   369→
   370→        // Brief LED flash
   371→        digitalWrite(LED_PIN, LOW);
   372→        vTaskDelay(100);
   373→        digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH);
   374→
   375→        // Stay in command mode for more commands
   376→        // Or switch back: is_wake_mode = true; afe_handle->enable_wakenet(afe_data);
   377→      }
   378→    }
   379→  }
   380→
   381→  vTaskDelete(NULL);
   382→}
   383→
   384→void handleCommand(int cmd_id) {
   385→  switch (cmd_id) {
   386→    case SR_CMD_LIGHT_ON:  Serial.println("  -> Light ON");  break;
   387→    case SR_CMD_LIGHT_OFF: Serial.println("  -> Light OFF"); break;
   388→    case SR_CMD_RED:       Serial.println("  -> RED");       break;
   389→    case SR_CMD_GREEN:     Serial.println("  -> GREEN");     break;
   390→    case SR_CMD_BLUE:      Serial.println("  -> BLUE");      break;
   391→    case SR_CMD_START:     Serial.println("  -> START");     break;
   392→    case SR_CMD_STOP:      Serial.println("  -> STOP");      break;
   393→    default:               Serial.println("  -> Unknown");   break;
   394→  }
   395→}

   453→void loop() {
   454→  // Blink LED slowly when listening for wake word
   455→  if (is_wake_mode) {
   456→    static unsigned long last_blink = 0;
   457→    if (millis() - last_blink > 1000) {
   458→      last_blink = millis();

   461→  }

   463→  delay(100);

    33→// Memory stream for PSRAM playback
    34→class MemoryStream : public Stream {
    35→  uint8_t *buf;
    36→  size_t sz, pos;
    37→public:
    38→  MemoryStream(uint8_t *b, size_t s) : buf(b), sz(s), pos(0) {}
    39→  int available() override { return sz - pos; }
    40→  int read() override { return (pos < sz) ? buf[pos++] : -1; }
    41→  int peek() override { return (pos < sz) ? buf[pos] : -1; }
    42→  size_t readBytes(char *b, size_t len) override {
    43→    size_t n = min(len, sz - pos);
    44→    memcpy(b, buf + pos, n);
    45→    pos += n;
    46→    return n;
    47→  }
    48→  void reset() { pos = 0; }
    49→  size_t write(uint8_t) override { return 0; }
    50→  void flush() override {}

    52→
    53→// Orientation manager with debounced rotation detection
    54→class OrientationManager {
    55→  const float THRESHOLD = 0.5;           // Hysteresis threshold (±0.5g)
    56→  const unsigned long DEBOUNCE_MS = 1000; // 1 second stability required
    57→  const unsigned long POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 50; // Poll at 20Hz
    58→
    59→  uint8_t currentRotation;    // Stable rotation: 1 (USB right) or 3 (USB left)
    60→  uint8_t pendingRotation;    // Candidate rotation during debounce (0 = none)
    61→  unsigned long debounceStartTime;
    62→  unsigned long lastPollTime;
    63→  bool rotationJustChanged;   // One-shot flag for change detection
    64→  bool imuAvailable;
    65→
    66→public:
    67→  OrientationManager() : currentRotation(1), pendingRotation(0),
    68→                         debounceStartTime(0), lastPollTime(0),
    69→                         rotationJustChanged(false), imuAvailable(true) {}
    70→
    71→  void setImuAvailable(bool available) {
    72→    imuAvailable = available;
    73→  }
    74→
    75→  void update() {
    76→    if (!imuAvailable) return;
    77→
    78→    unsigned long now = millis();
    79→    if (now - lastPollTime < POLL_INTERVAL_MS) return;
    80→    lastPollTime = now;
    81→
    82→    // Read accelerometer
    83→    IMU.update();
    84→    IMU.getAccel(&accelData);
    85→    float accelY = accelData.accelY;
    86→
    87→    // Determine desired rotation based on accelY
    88→    uint8_t desiredRotation = 0;
    89→    if (accelY > THRESHOLD) {
    90→      desiredRotation = 1;  // USB on right (normal)
    91→    } else if (accelY < -THRESHOLD) {
    92→      desiredRotation = 3;  // USB on left (180° flip)
    93→    } else {
    94→      desiredRotation = currentRotation; // Hysteresis zone - keep current
    95→    }
    96→
    97→    // State machine logic
    98→    if (desiredRotation == currentRotation) {
    99→      // Orientation matches current stable state
   100→      pendingRotation = 0; // Cancel any pending transition
   101→    } else if (pendingRotation == 0) {
   102→      // Start new transition
   103→      pendingRotation = desiredRotation;
   104→      debounceStartTime = now;
   105→    } else if (pendingRotation == desiredRotation) {
   106→      // Transition in progress, check if debounce time elapsed
   107→      if (now - debounceStartTime >= DEBOUNCE_MS) {
   108→        // Commit rotation change
   109→        currentRotation = pendingRotation;
   110→        pendingRotation = 0;
   111→        rotationJustChanged = true;
   112→      }
   113→    } else {
   114→      // Desired rotation changed during debounce - restart
   115→      pendingRotation = desiredRotation;
   116→      debounceStartTime = now;
   117→    }
   118→  }
   119→
   120→  uint8_t getRotation() {

   122→  }
   123→
   124→  bool hasChanged() {

   126→      rotationJustChanged = false; // Clear one-shot flag
   127→      return true;
   128→    }
   129→    return false;
   130→  }
   131→};

    14→ * GND ────────────┼────── GND ──────────┬─────── GND
    15→ *                 │                     │
    16→ * GPIO 2 (BCK) ───┼────── SCK ──────────┼─────── SCK
    17→ * GPIO 4 (WS) ────┼────── WS ───────────┼─────── WS
    18→ * GPIO 18 (DIN) ──┴────── SD ───────────┴─────── SD
    19→ *                         │                      │
    20→ *                         L/R → GND              L/R → 3.3V
    21→ *                           (LEFT)                 (RIGHT)
    22→ *
    23→ * Behavior:
    24→ * =========
    25→ * 1. On boot, allocates PSRAM buffer (~1.92 MB)
    26→ * 2. Initializes I2S in stereo mode
    27→ * 3. Records 30 seconds of audio to PSRAM (no SD interference!)
    28→ * 4. Mounts SD card
    29→ * 5. Writes complete recording to SD card
    30→ * 6. Prints completion message
    31→ * 7. Enters idle loop
    32→ *
    33→ * Output File:
    34→ * ============
    35→ * Format: WAV (PCM)
    36→ * Sample Rate: 16000 Hz
    37→ * Channels: 2 (Stereo)
    38→ * Bit Depth: 16-bit
    39→ * Duration: 30 seconds
    40→ * Size: ~1.92 MB
    41→ * Location: SD card root (/recording.wav)
    42→ */

    58→#define SD_SCK   39    // Serial Clock
    59→
    60→// Recording Configuration
    61→#define I2S_PORT        I2S_NUM_0
    62→#define SAMPLE_RATE     16000
    63→#define CHANNELS        2
    64→#define BITS_PER_SAMPLE 16
    65→#define RECORD_DURATION 30     // seconds
    66→#define BUFFER_SIZE     2048   // samples (int16_t stereo pairs)
    67→
    68→// Calculate total samples
    69→const uint32_t TOTAL_SAMPLES = SAMPLE_RATE * CHANNELS * RECORD_DURATION;
    70→const uint32_t WAV_DATA_SIZE = TOTAL_SAMPLES * (BITS_PER_SAMPLE / 8);

# ESP-SR Wake Word Detection (SD Card Models)

Loads ESP-SR speech recognition models from SD card into PSRAM at runtime, avoiding the need for special partition schemes.

## Setup

### 1. Copy Model File to SD Card

Copy the `srmodels.bin` file to the root of your SD card:

**Source location:**
\```
~/.arduino15/packages/esp32/tools/esp32-arduino-libs/idf-release_v5.5-07e9bf49-v1/esp32s3/esp_sr/srmodels.bin
\```

**On Linux/Mac:**
\```bash
cp ~/.arduino15/packages/esp32/tools/esp32-arduino-libs/idf-release_v5.5-*/esp32s3/esp_sr/srmodels.bin /path/to/sdcard/
\```

**On Windows:**
\```
%LOCALAPPDATA%\Arduino15\packages\esp32\tools\esp32-arduino-libs\idf-release_v5.5-*\esp32s3\esp_sr\srmodels.bin
\```

The file is ~2.4MB and contains both WakeNet and MultiNet models.

### 2. Arduino IDE Settings

| Setting | Value |
|---------|-------|
| Board | ESP32S3 Dev Module |
| Partition Scheme | **Your existing scheme** (e.g., 16MB 3MB APP/9MB FATFS) |
| PSRAM | OPI PSRAM |
| Flash Size | 16MB |

No special partition scheme required!

### 3. Hardware

**Microphones (INMP441):**
\```
ESP32-S3          INMP441 #1 (LEFT)      INMP441 #2 (RIGHT)
────────          ─────────────────      ──────────────────
3.3V ─────────┬── VDD                    VDD
              │
GND ──────────┼── GND ───────────┬────── GND
              │                  │
GPIO 2 ───────┼── SCK ───────────┼────── SCK
GPIO 4 ────────┼── WS ───────────┼────── WS
GPIO 18 ──────┴── SD ────────────┴────── SD
                  │                      │
                  L/R → GND              L/R → 3.3V
                    (LEFT)                 (RIGHT)
\```

**SD Card:** Uses built-in SD slot (SPI: CS=41, MOSI=38, MISO=40, SCK=39)

## Usage

1. Insert SD card with `srmodels.bin` at root
2. Upload sketch
3. Open Serial Monitor at 115200 baud
4. Say **"Hi ESP"** to wake up
5. After wake, speak a command within ~6 seconds

## Wake Word

**"Hi ESP"** (built into the model)

## Voice Commands

After wake word detection:

| Command | Aliases | Action |
|---------|---------|--------|
| "Turn on the light" | "Switch on the light" | Light ON |
| "Turn off the light" | "Switch off the light", "Go dark" | Light OFF |
| "Red" | - | RED |
| "Green" | - | GREEN |
| "Blue" | - | BLUE |
| "Start" | - | START |
| "Stop" | - | STOP |

## LED Feedback

| LED State | Meaning |
|-----------|---------|
| Slow blink (1s) | Listening for wake word |
| Solid ON | Wake word detected, listening for command |
| Fast blink (100ms) | Error |

## Serial Output Example

\```
========================================
ESP-SR Wake Word Demo (SD Card Models)
========================================

PSRAM: 8257536 / 8388608 bytes free
Heap:  320000 / 327680 bytes free

Initializing SD card SPI... OK
Mounting SD card... OK
Opening /srmodels.bin... OK
Model size: 2446336 bytes
Allocating PSRAM... OK
Loading model to PSRAM... OK
Parsing models... OK (3 models found)
  - wn9_hiesp
  - mn5_en
  - nsnet2

Initializing I2S... OK
Initializing AFE... OK
Initializing MultiNet... using mn5_en... OK

Voice commands (after wake word):
  - 'Turn on the light'
  - 'Switch on the light'
  - 'Turn off the light'
  ...

Feed task started (chunksize=512)
Detect task started

Listening for wake word 'Hi ESP'...

*** WAKE WORD DETECTED! ***
Wake verified (channel 0)
Listening for command...

Command: 'Turn on the light' (id=0, conf=0.95)
  -> Light ON
\```

## Troubleshooting

### "Mounting SD card... FAILED"
- Check SD card is inserted
- Format as FAT32
- Try a different SD card

### "Opening /srmodels.bin... FAILED"
- Copy `srmodels.bin` to SD card root
- Check filename is exactly `srmodels.bin`

### "Parsing models... FAILED"
- Model file may be corrupted
- Re-copy from Arduino packages folder

### "Initializing AFE... FAILED"
- Insufficient PSRAM
- Check PSRAM is enabled in board settings

### Wake word not detected
- Speak clearly: "Hi ESP" (Hi E-S-P)
- Move closer to microphone
- Check mic wiring (BCK=2, WS=4, DIN=18)

## How It Works

1. **SD Card Loading**: Reads `srmodels.bin` (2.4MB) into PSRAM at boot
2. **Model Parsing**: `srmodel_load()` parses the binary into model structures
3. **AFE Init**: Audio Front End processes stereo mic input (noise reduction, etc.)
4. **WakeNet**: Detects "Hi ESP" wake word
5. **MultiNet**: After wake, recognizes voice commands using phoneme matching
6. **Dual-Core**: Feed task on Core 0, Detect task on Core 1

## Adding Custom Commands

To add custom commands, generate phoneme strings:

\```bash
pip3 install g2p_en

cd ~/.arduino15/packages/esp32/hardware/esp32/3.3.2/libraries/ESP_SR/tools
python3 gen_sr_commands.py "Hello world;Goodbye"
\```

Add the output to the `commands[]` array in the sketch.

## Memory Usage

| Component | Size | Location |
|-----------|------|----------|
| Model file | ~2.4 MB | PSRAM |
| AFE buffers | ~500 KB | PSRAM + heap |
| Audio buffers | ~32 KB | Heap |
| Feed task stack | 4 KB | Heap |
| Detect task stack | 8 KB | Heap |

Total PSRAM usage: ~3 MB

## Technical Details

- Sample rate: 16 kHz
- Bit depth: 16-bit
- Channels: 2 (stereo)
- Wake word model: WakeNet 9 ("Hi ESP")
- Command model: MultiNet 5 (English)
- AFE mode: Low cost (optimized for single speaker)

## ESP-SR Custom Wake Word Training Options

Espressif offers two ways to customize the wake word: the Espressif Speech Wake Words Customization Process or Training Wake Words by TTS sample.

### Option 1: Espressif Official Customization Service

It usually takes two to three weeks for Espressif to train and optimize the received corpus, and a fee will be charged for training and optimizing the corpus.

**Corpus Requirements if providing your own:**
- Number of samples: more than 500 people, including men and women of all ages and at least 100 children.
- Sampling environment: a quiet room (< 40 dB). It is recommended to use a professional audio room. Recording device: high-fidelity microphone.
- At 1 meter away from the microphone: each person speaks the wake word out loud for 15 times (5 times in fast speed, 5 times in normal speed, 5 times in slow speed). At 3 meters away from the microphone: each person speaks the wake word out loud for 15 times as well.

### Option 2: TTS-Based Training (Self-Service)

Models with "_tts" suffix mean the WakeNet model is trained by TTS samples. "_tts2" suffix means the WakeNet model is trained by TTS Pipeline V2.(no content)A more powerful TTS (Text-to-Speech) model has been integrated, enhancing the performance of wake word training. The updated system now achieves accuracy comparable to models trained with human samples, with performance ranging from 95% to 98%.

### Recent Updates (2025)

- ESP-SR V2.0 was released on February 14, 2025.
- VADNet, a voice activity detection model, was released on February 13, 2025. You can use it to replace the WebRTC VAD and improve performance.
- A new model WakeNet9s was added on April 21, 2025, which can run on chips that do not have PSRAM and do not support SIMD, such as ESP32C3 and ESP32C5.
- WakeNet9l was added on October 20, 2025, which further improves the response rate of wake words spoken at extremely fast speeds based on WakeNet9, but its CPU and memory requirements are approximately 1.3 times higher.

### Supported Models

The WakeNet engine enables devices to always listen for wake words such as "Alexa", "Hi,lexin" and "Hi,ESP". WakeNet9 and WakeNet9s models are supported. WakeNet9s is a cost-down version of WakeNet9, with fewer parameters and lower computational requirements.(no content)Espressif provides wake words such as "Hi, Lexin" and "Hi, ESP" for free, and also supports custom wake words.

### Resources
- Official documentation: https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-sr/
- GitHub repository: https://github.com/espressif/esp-sr
- ESP-Skainet examples: https://github.com/espressif/esp-skainet

# Wake Word Customization Options

Based on the documentation, Espressif offers **two primary customization paths**:

## Service-Based Training (Not Self-Service)

Espressif does not provide TTS-based or self-service training options. Instead, they offer:

1. **Customer-Provided Corpus**: Customers supply training data (minimum 20,000 qualified samples) with "two to three weeks" for processing and optimization, plus associated fees.

2. **Espressif-Provided Corpus**: Espressif collects all necessary training data, requiring separate discussion on timeline and carrying "a fee...for collecting the corpus" plus optimization costs.

## Key Limitations

The documentation specifies that "currently, up to 5 wake words are supported by each WakeNet model" and emphasizes that "the actual fee and time...depend on the number of wake words" and production scale—requiring direct contact with their sales team.

**No local or self-service TTS-based training capability is mentioned.** The process requires engaging Espressif's professional services with associated costs and timeline negotiations.

# WakeNet Wake Word Models Overview

## Available Wake Word Models

The documentation identifies several WakeNet generations, with the following currently supported:

**WakeNet9 and WakeNet9l** support ESP32, ESP32S3, and ESP32P4 chips, built on "Dilated Convolution" architecture. WakeNet9l specifically enhances recognition for rapidly-spoken wake words.

**WakeNet9s** is designed for ESP32C3, ESP32C5, and ESP32C6 chips, utilizing "Depthwise Separable Convolution" structure.

Earlier versions (WakeNet1-8) are noted as obsolete.

## Key Findings

### openWakeWord and ESP32 Limitations
openWakeWord is generally small and efficient, but likely not enough to be suitable for deployment on very low power edge devices. For example, some experimentation by other openWakeWord users & contributors indicates that it may still take several seconds to process a single 80 ms frame on an ESP32-S3 with quantized openWakeWord models.(no content)Instead, the openWakeWord author recommends the excellent microWakeWord library from @kahrendt. It uses a similar synthetic-only training data approach and can produce high quality models that are efficient enough to run on very low power edge devices.

### microWakeWord - The ESP32-Optimized Alternative
Kevin Ahrendt has written microWakeWord to develop streaming wake word models suitable for ESP32-S3 devices. ESPHome's February 2024 release added support for microWakeWord models.(no content)The streaming model performs inferences every 20 ms on the newest audio stride. The model is based on an inception neural network converted for streaming. It executes an inference in under 10 ms on an ESP32-S3.

### Custom Wake Word Training
It is currently not trivial to train a new model. The developer is working on a custom training framework to make the process much easier.(no content)For training, positive and negative samples are generated using openWakeWord, which relies on Piper sample generator. They also use openWakeWord's data tools to augment the positive and negative samples.

### Home Assistant Self-Hosted Integration
For self-hosted setups, you can open the share folder and create a new folder `/share/openwakeword`, then drop your custom wake word model file (.tflite) into that folder.(no content)Unfortunately, openWakeWord was too large to run on low power devices like S3-BOX-3. So wake word detection runs inside Home Assistant instead. This allows tiny devices like the M5 ATOM Echo Development Kit to simply stream audio and let all of the processing happen elsewhere.

### 2024 Model Updates
The newer models are faster and more accurate. Up to 3 models can run on a regular ESP32 at the same time (e.g., VAD, "okay nabu", and "hey mycroft"). ESP32-S3 supports running all 4 concurrently.

### Key Resources
- **openWakeWord GitHub**: https://github.com/dscripka/openWakeWord
- **microWakeWord for ESP32**: https://github.com/kahrendt/esphome-on-device-wake-word
- **OHF-Voice micro-wake-word releases**: https://github.com/OHF-Voice/micro-wake-word/releases
- **ESPHome Documentation**: https://esphome.io/components/micro_wake_word/
- **Home Assistant Wake Word Guide**: https://www.home-assistant.io/voice_control/create_wake_word/

Here's the landscape for custom wake words on ESP32:

## ESP-SR Custom Wake Word Options

### Option 1: Espressif Official Service (Paid)
- **Process**: Contact Espressif sales, provide ~20,000+ audio samples or pay for corpus collection
- **Timeline**: 2-3 weeks
- **Cost**: Fee for training + optimization
- **Result**: Professional WakeNet model embedded in `srmodels.bin`
- **Not self-service** - requires business engagement

### Option 2: TTS-Trained Models (Limited)
Some models have `_tts` suffix (trained with synthetic speech). Espressif may offer this for some common words, but still requires their service.

---

## Better Alternative: microWakeWord (You Already Have This!)

Looking at your codebase, you already have `workbench/tests/wakeword_pretrained_test/` which uses **microWakeWord** - a much better path for custom wake words:

| Feature | ESP-SR WakeNet | microWakeWord |
|---------|----------------|---------------|
| Custom training | Paid service only | Self-trainable |
| Model format | Proprietary binary | Standard TFLite |
| Pre-trained models | "Hi ESP", "Alexa" | "Hey Jarvis", "OK Nabu", etc. |
| Training data | Real human audio | Synthetic (Piper TTS) |
| Runs on ESP32-S3 | Yes | Yes (~10ms inference) |

### microWakeWord Training Pipeline

```
[Custom wake word text]
        ↓
[Piper TTS] → generates synthetic positive samples
        ↓
[openWakeWord tools] → augments with noise, reverb, etc.
        ↓
[Training] → produces .tflite model
        ↓
[ESP32-S3] → runs inference via TFLite Micro
```

### Pre-trained Models Available
From [OHF-Voice/micro-wake-word](https://github.com/OHF-Voice/micro-wake-word/releases):
- "Hey Jarvis"
- "OK Nabu"  
- "Hey Mycroft"
- "Alexa"
- And more...

---

## Recommendation

For a custom wake word like "Hey OAISYS":

1. **Use microWakeWord approach** (TFLite-based, already in your codebase)
2. Training requires:
   - [Piper TTS](https://github.com/rhasspy/piper) to generate synthetic samples
   - [openWakeWord data tools](https://github.com/dscripka/openWakeWord) for augmentation
   - Training script (still being simplified by the microWakeWord author)

3. **Alternatively**: Start with a pre-trained model like "Hey Jarvis" from your existing test, then explore custom training later.

---
